description: These two tables give, for every municipality in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua, the average time needed to reach the nearest health centre, one by motor vehicle and one on foot. The producer is Action Against Hunger (Acción contra el Hambre) with its GIS4Tech team, which also runs the PREDISAN health planning platform. Coverage is these four Central American countries, with values for 2020 based on facility data taken from the Humanitarian Data Exchange in June 2020, organised by country, department and municipality. Health centres include clinics, hospitals, outpatient clinics and other health centres. The files are available as free CSV downloads under a Creative Commons Attribution licence, with more detail on the PREDISAN platform. Caveats: averages hide the spread within large municipalities, facility locations come from secondary open data of uneven completeness, capacity and opening hours are ignored, and the method is described only briefly. Simulation uses: identifying municipalities where hazards that cut roads would isolate people from care, baseline access for health planning, and comparison with model-based travel-time grids. Related records: the Malaria Atlas Project travel time maps (data-map-travel-time-to-healthcare) and the HeiGIT accessibility indicators (data-heigit-accessibility-indicators).
